source_topic: Price, volume and unit-cost profit bridge

follow_up.question: Which interaction can an additive percentage bridge miss?
follow_up.reference: A price change applies to the new unit volume, so price and volume effects interact. Unit-cost changes also apply to the changed volume; rebuilding the two profit statements captures those interactions.

instances.text: You assess a manufacturer's price and efficiency plan. Initially, annual sales are 70 thousand units at 50 dollars each, variable cost is 30 dollars per unit, and fixed operating cost is 140 thousand dollars. Next year, price falls by 20 percent, unit volume falls by 10 percent, and unit variable cost falls by 10 percent. Apply each change to its original base; the stated volume change already reflects the price change. Annual fixed cost increases by 70 thousand dollars. Ignore tax, financing and other changes. What is the signed change in annual operating profit, in thousands of dollars?
